$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =-5-7(x-4) \\  & =-5-7x+28 \\  & =-7x+23.\end{aligned}

The third-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =f(4)+{f}^{′}(4)(x-4)+\frac{{f}^{″}(4)}{2!}(x-4)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(4)}{3!}(x-4)^{3} \\  & =f(4)+{f}^{′}(4)(x-4)+\frac{{f}^{″}(4)}{2}(x-4)^{2}+\frac{{f}^{‴}(4)}{6}(x-4)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We have the following set of values:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4)=-5 \\ {f}^{′}(4)=-7 \\ {f}^{″}(4)=-10 \\ {f}^{‴}(4)=-13\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the given values into our Taylor Polynomial, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{3}(x) & =-5-7(x-4)+\frac{(-10)}{2}(x-4)^{2}+\frac{(-13)}{6}(x-4)^{3} \\  & =-5-7(x-4)-5(x-4)^{2}-\frac{13}{6}(x-4)^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
According to the Lagrange error bound, the third-degree Taylor polynomial for $f(x)$ about $x=4$ approximates $f(3.9)$ with an error that is less than{{field-1}}
(Do not round your answer, write it as a fraction).
questions.worked_solution:
The Lagrange error bound states that an upper bound for the error ${R}_{3}$ obtained when using the third-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{3}$ to approximate $f(x)$ is given by

$$
|{R}_{3}|\le \frac{M}{4!}|x-4{|}^{4},
$$

where $M$ is the maximum value of $|{f}^{(4)}(x)|$ on the interval between $a=4$ and $x=3.91.$ Plugging $x=3.9$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}|{R}_{3}|\le \frac{M}{4!}|3.9-4{|}^{4} \\ |{R}_{3}|\le \frac{M}{24}|-0.1{|}^{4} \\ |{R}_{3}|\le \frac{M}{24}(0.1)^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find $M,$ we need to find the maximum of $|{f}^{(4)}(x)|$ on the interval $[3.9,4].$

Since $f$ and all its derivatives are decreasing on the interval $[2,4],$ and since ${f}^{(4)}(x)$ is negative in this interval, we know that $|{f}^{(4)}(x)|$ is an increasing function on the interval $[3.9,4]$ and its value is greatest at $x=4.$ So

$$
M=|{f}^{(4)}(4)|=|-6|=6,
$$

and therefore, the upper bound is

$$
|{R}_{3}|\le \frac{6}{24}(0.1)^{4}=\frac{1}{40\,000}.
$$
